verdict.rationale: GitLab's marketing says it includes a Secret Detection scanner among its consolidated scanners, shows security findings in merge requests and IDEs, and has agents that can remediate vulnerabilities. That covers detection in principle, but the evidence is only one-line homepage claims with no detail on organization-wide coverage or on remediating leaked secrets specifically. Missing for 10: documented org/group-wide secret scanning across all repositories, scanning of existing git history, secret-specific remediation workflows (revoking or rotating leaked credentials, push protection), in-depth first-party Secret Detection docs, independent or hands-on corroboration.
